conflicts.description: The same movie/title entity is named title_basics in the IMDB schema and film in the Sakila schema; film_text is a denormalized duplicate of the same concept.
conflicts.resolution: Merged under a single resource named title, absorbing film_text as a denormalized duplicate.

conflicts.description: The same person entity is called name_basics in IMDB and actor in Sakila.
conflicts.resolution: Merged under a single resource named person.

conflicts.description: Title identifiers (tconst vs film_id) and person identifiers (nconst vs actor_id) use different column names for the same identity.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed to neutral title_id and person_id respectively.

conflicts.description: Equivalent attributes carry divergent names across schemas (startyear/release_year, runtimeminutes/length, primarytitle/title).
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to release_year, runtime_minutes and primary_title.

conflicts.description: The film classification taxonomy is named category in Sakila and genres in IMDB.
conflicts.resolution: Unified as genre with a shared name attribute.

conflicts.description: The token rating is a homonym: in IMDB it denotes a numeric user score, in Sakila it denotes an MPAA-style content rating.
conflicts.resolution: Disambiguated into separate attributes average_rating (numeric score) and content_rating (age/classification rating).

conflicts.description: IMDB models identifiers as number while Sakila models them as string (and some Sakila FK columns as integer).
conflicts.resolution: All identifiers standardized to string, since IMDB identifiers are alphanumeric and references must match.

conflicts.description: Runtime is typed as string in film.length but integer in title_basics.runtimeminutes.
conflicts.resolution: Cast to integer runtime_minutes (values expressed in minutes).

conflicts.description: All year attributes are typed as string in the sources, using a null sentinel for missing values.
conflicts.resolution: Converted to integer, mapping the null sentinel to null.

conflicts.description: Boolean flags are represented as string in the sources.
conflicts.resolution: Converted to boolean.

conflicts.description: Monetary values are typed as string in the sources.
conflicts.resolution: Converted to number.

conflicts.description: Date-time values are typed as date despite descriptions stating date and time.
conflicts.resolution: Typed as datetime to preserve the time component; pure date columns (last_update, create_date) remain date.

conflicts.description: title_basics.primarytitle is typed as integer although it holds textual title content.
conflicts.resolution: Corrected to string.

conflicts.description: Boolean attributes are documented as 0/1 integer codes.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized to boolean.

conflicts.description: Language is encoded as an ISO code in title_akas.language but as an English name in sakila.language.name; different encodings of the same dimension.
conflicts.resolution: Sakila retains language_id/name as the canonical language dimension; the IMDB alias language is kept as a distinct language_code attribute to avoid conflating code and name.

conflicts.description: The two genre/category taxonomies use overlapping but non-identical value sets (e.g. IMDB Drama vs Sakila Classics).
conflicts.resolution: Merged into a single genre dimension matched by name, accepting that the combined value space is broader than either source.

conflicts.description: Boolean semantics are encoded inconsistently (0/1 integers vs TRUE/FALSE strings).
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to a single boolean representation with true/false semantics.

conflicts.description: Both measure duration; IMDB uses an explicit minutes unit in the name, Sakila an implicit one.
conflicts.resolution: Kept as runtime_minutes with an explicit, consistent minutes unit.

conflicts.description: Missing values are encoded with a string sentinel in the IMDB year columns.
conflicts.resolution: Sentinel values reinterpreted as null in numeric target columns.

conflicts.description: Person-title involvement is modeled three different ways: multi-valued arrays (title_crew.directors/writers), an attributed credit table (title_principals with category/job/characters), and a plain junction table (film_actor).
conflicts.resolution: Normalized into a single title_credit resource capturing person, title, role, job and characters; crew arrays are exploded into one row per person with a fixed role.

conflicts.description: Genres are a multi-valued column in IMDB but a fully normalized many-to-many structure in Sakila.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized into genre plus a title_genre junction table.

conflicts.description: A person notable titles are stored as an array of title identifiers.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized into the person_known_for_title junction table.

conflicts.description: A person professions are stored as an array of strings.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized into the person_profession child table.

conflicts.description: film_text denormalizes film title and description into a separate search table.
conflicts.resolution: Folded into the title resource; the duplicate columns were mapped onto the same target attributes.

conflicts.description: Episode relationships and ratings are held in separate 1:1 side tables in IMDB rather than embedded attributes.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved as dedicated title_episode and title_rating resources to keep the title entity normalized.

conflicts.description: Person names are stored as a single unsplit string in IMDB but split into first/last components in Sakila.
conflicts.resolution: Retained both representations (primary_name and first_name/last_name) to preserve information from either source.

conflicts.description: Title-to-genre is N:M in Sakila (junction table) but an unbounded multi-value field in IMDB.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as an N:M relationship via the title_genre junction table.

conflicts.description: Person-to-title involvement is N:M across all sources.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as an N:M relationship via the title_credit table.

conflicts.description: A title has many alternative titles (1:N).
conflicts.resolution: Preserved as a 1:N child resource title_aka keyed by (title_id, ordering).

conflicts.description: A TV series has many episodes (1:N self-referencing relationship).
conflicts.resolution: Preserved via title_episode with title_id and parent_title_id both referencing title.

conflicts.description: Ratings relate to a title 1:1.
conflicts.resolution: Kept as a 1:1 side table title_rating keyed by title_id.

conflicts.description: Persons and their known-for titles form an N:M relationship.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as N:M via person_known_for_title.

conflicts.description: title_akas declares no primary key, though (titleid, ordering) uniquely identifies rows.
conflicts.resolution: Composite primary key defined as (title_id, ordering).

conflicts.description: Several source resources declare no primary key, leaving their identity ambiguous.
conflicts.resolution: Natural/composite keys were assigned where derivable (title_episode.title_id, title_rating.title_id, title_genre composite, title_aka composite) and a synthetic surrogate credit_id was introduced for title_credit.

conflicts.description: IMDB uses a natural alphanumeric key (tconst) while Sakila uses a surrogate key (film_id) for the same title entity.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into title_id whose provenance lists both source keys.

conflicts.description: IMDB uses a natural key (nconst) while Sakila uses a surrogate key (actor_id) for the same person entity.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into person_id whose provenance lists both source keys.

conflicts.description: film_text.film_id is a de facto foreign key to film but no foreign key is declared.
conflicts.resolution: Treated as an alias of the title identifier and folded into title_id.

conflicts.description: The person entity is named 'name_basics' in IMDB and 'actor' in Sakila, and the primary identifier is 'nconst' vs 'actor_id'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into a single 'person' resource with 'person_id', merging both identity columns.

conflicts.description: The title/film entity is named 'title_basics' in IMDB and 'film' in Sakila; identifiers are 'tconst' vs 'film_id' and the headline title is 'primarytitle' vs 'title'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into a 'title' resource with 'title_id' and 'primary_title'; source names retained only in source_provenance.

conflicts.description: Generic labels ('name', 'title', 'types') are reused for different concepts across the two schemas (category name, language name, alias title).
conflicts.resolution: Disambiguated by qualifying target field names (e.g. content_rating, content category 'name' vs alias 'title').

conflicts.description: 'film_text' replicates 'film' under a different name, representing the same entity (denormalized duplicate).
conflicts.resolution: Folded into the 'title' resource; its 'title' and 'description' columns contribute to the corresponding target fields.

conflicts.description: The actor-title relationship is named 'film_actor' in Sakila and 'title_principals' in IMDB for the same conceptual credit relationship.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into a single 'title_credit' resource.

conflicts.description: IMDB declares alphanumeric identifiers as 'number' while Sakila declares surrogate identifiers as 'string'; both are non-numeric keys.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized all identifiers (title_id, person_id, and all FK ids) to 'string'.

conflicts.description: 'primarytitle' is declared 'integer' although it holds a textual title (source mis-typing).
conflicts.resolution: Re-typed to 'string' in 'title.primary_title'.

conflicts.description: All year attributes are stored as 'string' (YYYY) in the sources.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized to 'integer' years (birth_year, death_year, start_year, end_year).

conflicts.description: Runtime is declared 'string' in Sakila but 'integer' in IMDB.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized to the integer field 'runtime_minutes'.

conflicts.description: Monetary and duration quantities are declared as 'string' although they are numeric.
conflicts.resolution: Re-typed to 'number' (rental_rate, replacement_cost, amount) and 'integer' (rental_duration).

conflicts.description: Boolean semantics are encoded as 'string' in Sakila (active) but as 'boolean' in IMDB (isadult, isoriginaltitle).
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'boolean' for all flags (active, is_adult, is_original_title).

conflicts.description: Temporal columns carrying a time component are declared as 'date'.
conflicts.resolution: Promoted to 'datetime' (rental_date, return_date, payment_date); pure calendar columns remain 'date'.

conflicts.description: Both are labelled 'rating' but represent different semantics: a 0–10 weighted numeric average vs an MPAA categorical rating (G/PG/PG-13/R/NC-17).
conflicts.resolution: Kept as separate fields, 'average_rating' (number) and 'content_rating' (string); no cross-mapping performed.

conflicts.description: 'genres' (IMDB) and 'category' (Sakila) are both title classifications but use different, non-identical vocabularies.
conflicts.resolution: Kept as distinct structures ('title_genre' string list vs 'category'/'title_category' dimension) rather than merged into one taxonomy.

conflicts.description: Language is represented as a free-text name/code in IMDB's alias table but as a normalized dimension reference in Sakila.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved distinctly: 'title_alias.language' stays a string attribute while Sakila languages become the 'language' dimension referenced by title FKs.

conflicts.description: Two different durations coexist (runtime in minutes vs rental period in days) and could be confused.
conflicts.resolution: Materialized as separate atomic fields 'runtime_minutes' and 'rental_duration' with distinct units/meaning.

conflicts.description: Sakila's actor link implies a fixed role ('actor') whereas IMDB's principals encode an explicit category/job attribute.
conflicts.resolution: Unified rows carry an optional 'category'; actor-only rows leave known-role attributes null without inventing derived categorical values.

conflicts.description: IMDB embeds array/multi-value attributes inside single columns, whereas Sakila normalizes relationships into separate tables.
conflicts.resolution: Multi-valued relationships were normalized into bridge tables (person_known_for, title_genre, title_director, title_writer, title_credit); free-text attribute arrays (types, attributes, characters, primary_profession) are retained as string fields.

conflicts.description: Sakila uses dedicated bridge tables for film-actor and film-category many-to-many structures.
conflicts.resolution: film_actor was merged into the unified 'title_credit' bridge; film_category maps to the 'title_category' bridge, preserving the normalized design.

conflicts.description: 'film_text' duplicates 'film' columns (film_id, title, description) creating redundancy and potential inconsistency.
conflicts.resolution: Removed as a duplicate; its columns were absorbed into the 'title' resource as additional provenance.

conflicts.description: Sakila separates person-like data into actor, customer and staff tables whereas IMDB keeps a single person table.
conflicts.resolution: 'actor' was merged with 'name_basics' into 'person'; 'customer' and 'staff' were retained as distinct entities because they model separate business roles with their own attributes.

conflicts.description: Title–person involvement is modeled with conflicting cardinality representations: title_crew stores arrays on a 1:1 title row while title_principals uses N rows per title.
conflicts.resolution: Both were decomposed into N:M bridge tables (title_director, title_writer, title_credit) so every relationship is many-to-many at the same grain.

conflicts.description: Three separate N:M title–person relationships (cast, principals, known-for) overlap conceptually.
conflicts.resolution: Cast and principals were merged into 'title_credit'; known-for remains a distinct relationship in 'person_known_for'.

conflicts.description: A self-referential series→episode hierarchy (1:N) exists in IMDB only.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as 'title_episode' with parent_title_id and title_id both referencing the 'title' resource.

conflicts.description: Title-to-classification is N:M in Sakila (via bridge) but embedded 1:many inside a single IMDB column.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the Sakila side as a bridge ('title_category') and the IMDB side as a comparable bridge ('title_genre').

conflicts.description: Sakila relates titles to a language dimension (N:1, twice) while IMDB carries language as a per-alias string.
conflicts.resolution: Foreign-key relationships (language_id, original_language_id) preserved for Sakila; the alias-level language string retained separately.

conflicts.description: Several source tables declare no primary key even though natural keys exist (e.g. title_akas: titleid+ordering; title_ratings: tconst; payment: payment_id).
conflicts.resolution: Inferred natural/composite keys and declared them as target primaryKeys ([title_id, ordering], title_id, [title_id, person_id], etc.).

conflicts.description: IMDB uses natural alphanumeric business keys while Sakila uses surrogate numeric keys; key types also differ (number vs string).
conflicts.resolution: Cross-source surrogate keys (title_id, person_id) unify the two key schemes, and both source keys are recorded in source_provenance.

conflicts.description: Two foreign keys in title_episode point to the same referenced entity (title_basics), a role-distinguished duplicate key situation.
conflicts.resolution: Both mapped to the same 'title' resource via distinct role-named columns (title_id and parent_title_id).

conflicts.description: film_text.film_id is a duplicated key of film.film_id with no declared PK or FK.
conflicts.resolution: Merged into the single 'title_id' key of the 'title' resource, eliminating the duplicate key.

conflicts.description: Foreign keys of different entity types (person vs title) risk being conflated across the merged bridge tables.
conflicts.resolution: Kept foreign keys semantically isolated: person identifiers only ever map to person_id (person), title identifiers only to title_id (title).

conflicts.description: The same real-world concept (an audiovisual work / motion picture) is named 'title_basics' in IMDb and 'film' in Sakila. The word 'title' is also overloaded in IMDb (title_basics.primarytitle, title_akas.title).
conflicts.resolution: Both entities are unified into a single resource named 'title'; the term 'title' is reserved for the work entity, its display name is renamed 'primary_title', and alternative-titles are renamed 'alternative_title'.

conflicts.description: The person entity is named 'name_basics' in IMDb and 'actor' in Sakila, though both represent individuals involved in productions.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into a single resource named 'person'.

conflicts.description: Homonym: 'category' denotes the job/role of a credited person in IMDb, but a film genre lookup table in Sakila.
conflicts.resolution: The IMDb concept is kept as the 'category' (role) column of 'title_credit'; the Sakila lookup is renamed and modeled as the 'genre' resource.

conflicts.description: Generic name columns ('name', 'city', 'country') are used to store the descriptive label of different lookups, causing name collisions across dimensions.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed to explicit, entity-qualified names: genre_name, language_name, city_name, country_name.

conflicts.description: The column name 'title' refers to four different things: the primary title, the localized alternative title, and (twice) the film title in two Sakila tables.
conflicts.resolution: Disambiguated into 'primary_title' (unified IMDb primarytitle + Sakila film/title_text title) and 'alternative_title' (IMDb title_akas title).

conflicts.description: The language concept is represented as an inline string column in IMDb and as an independent lookup table in Sakila.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as a shared 'language' dimension; IMDb's per-alt-title language is captured via a language_id foreign key.

conflicts.description: 'film_text' duplicates the film title and description under a different name.
conflicts.resolution: Recognized as a denormalized copy of 'film'; merged into 'title' and not materialized as a separate resource.

conflicts.description: 'region' (IMDb) and 'country' (Sakila) both denominate geographic areas but with different labelling and granularity.
conflicts.resolution: Kept distinct: 'region' remains a title-distribution attribute on 'title_alternative'; 'country' is modeled as a normalized dimension.

conflicts.description: IMDb identifier columns are declared as 'number' although their descriptions state they are alphanumeric strings (e.g. 'tt0000001', 'nm0000001').
conflicts.resolution: Re-typed to 'string' across all target resources.

conflicts.description: Year values are declared as 'string' (YYYY) in IMDb and as 'string' in Sakila even though they are numeric.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'integer' (birth_year, death_year, release_year, end_year).

conflicts.description: Declared as 'integer' although the description states it is the primary title string.
conflicts.resolution: Corrected to 'string' (primary_title).

conflicts.description: Sakila foreign-key columns are typed inconsistently: some 'integer' (film.language_id, address.city_id, inventory.film_id) while the referenced primary keys are 'string'.
conflicts.resolution: All identifier and foreign-key columns are uniformly typed as 'string'.

conflicts.description: Numeric measurements and money values are stored as 'string' in Sakila.
conflicts.resolution: Re-typed to 'integer' (rental_duration_days) and 'number' (rental_rate, replacement_cost, amount, runtime_minutes).

conflicts.description: Boolean flags are inconsistently typed: 'string' in Sakila (active) versus 'boolean' in IMDb (isadult, isoriginaltitle), and encoded as 0/1 in IMDb.
conflicts.resolution: All flags are typed 'boolean' (active, is_adult, is_original_title).

conflicts.description: Columns described as 'date and time' are typed 'date', losing the time component.
conflicts.resolution: Re-typed to 'datetime'.

conflicts.description: Sakila surrogate keys are declared as 'string' although they are integer surrogates, whereas IMDb uses alphanumeric natural keys.
conflicts.resolution: Uniformly typed 'string' to allow the merged keys of both sources to co-exist.

conflicts.description: Two different notions of 'rating': IMDb is a continuous weighted average (0-10), Sakila is a categorical age/MPAA rating (G, PG, PG-13, R, NC-17). Different scale and encoding.
conflicts.resolution: Kept as separate semantics: 'average_rating' (number) in the title_rating resource and 'content_rating' (string) on 'title'.

conflicts.description: Both express the runtime, and both use minutes as the unit; Sakila's column is however typed as string and unlabelled.
conflicts.resolution: Aligned on the common SI-friendly unit of minutes into a single 'runtime_minutes' integer column.

conflicts.description: IMDb encodes missing values with the literal '\N' inside year strings, which is a value-level encoding not representable once years become integers.
conflicts.resolution: The '\N' sentinel is normalized to a null value when casting years to integer.

conflicts.description: Same concept (language) encoded differently: IMDb uses ISO-like codes, Sakila uses English language names.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into a 'language' dimension; IMDb codes are harmonized to the dimension's identity while its name attribute carries the English label.

conflicts.description: Genre/category vocabularies differ between sources (IMDb's fixed genre set vs Sakila's rental-shop categories), and IMDb limits a title to three genres.
conflicts.resolution: Both are mapped into a single 'genre' dimension and a shared 'title_genre' bridge; vocabulary harmonization is left to a controlled value list.

conflicts.description: Active flags are documented to be set to 'FALSE' (rather than deleting rows), implying string/boolean ambiguity in encoding.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized to a real boolean type with a uniform true/false semantics.

conflicts.description: Geographic scope is represented at different granularities (distribution region, country dimension, and free-text district).
conflicts.resolution: Preserved as separate attributes at the correct granularity rather than forcing a lossy merge.

conflicts.description: IMDb stores many-to-many data as delimited/array values packed into a single column, whereas Sakila stores the same kinds of associations in fully normalized bridge tables.
conflicts.resolution: IMDb arrays are decomposed into bridge/child resources (title_genre, title_credit, person_profession, person_known_for) consistent with the normalized Sakila pattern; free-text arrays that are non-enumerated (attributes, types, characters) remain delimited strings.

conflicts.description: film_text is a denormalized projection of the film table (title + description keyed by film_id), introducing redundancy.
conflicts.resolution: Dropped as a separate resource; its columns are folded into 'title' with provenance retained.

conflicts.description: IMDb splits the title/person relationship across two tables of differing shape: title_crew packs director and writer arrays into one row per title, while title_principals holds one row per person credit.
conflicts.resolution: Both are unpivoted and unified into the row-per-credit 'title_credit' resource alongside Sakila's film_actor.

conflicts.description: Sakila has a normalized three-level location hierarchy that has no counterpart in IMDb.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved as separate country, city, and address resources, with foreign keys maintaining the hierarchy.

conflicts.description: IMDb models the series/episode relationship as a self-referencing association within a title-oriented table, unlike the flat Sakila model.
conflicts.resolution: Extracted into a dedicated 'title_episode' child resource with a self-referencing foreign key to 'title'.

conflicts.description: Sakila contains a complete rental/commerce domain (inventory, rental, payment, store, staff, customer) with no counterpart in IMDb.
conflicts.resolution: Retained as-is (normalized to the unified 'title' foreign key where it referenced 'film'), as these are legitimate domain-specific resources.

conflicts.description: The title-to-ratings relationship is 1:1 (a single ratings row per title), whereas most other audio-visual relationships are 1:N or N:M.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as a 1:1 extension resource 'title_rating' whose primary key is the title_id foreign key.

conflicts.description: Person-to-title is N:M in both sources but is expressed through different mechanisms and role semantics.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into the N:M 'title_credit' bridge between 'person' and 'title'.

conflicts.description: Sakila title-to-genre is a clean N:M bridge; IMDb embeds an inline array of up to three genres per title.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into the N:M 'title_genre' bridge.

conflicts.description: A TV series relates 1:N to its episodes, and each episode maps back to exactly one parent series.
conflicts.resolution: Represented via self-referencing foreign keys on 'title_episode'.

conflicts.description: Circular 1:N references between store and staff (a store has a manager staff member; a staff member belongs to a home store).
conflicts.resolution: Both foreign keys are retained in the unified schema; the cycle is preserved as-is.

conflicts.description: The 'known for' relationship is 1:N from a person to several titles in IMDb.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized into the 'person_known_for' resource linking person to title.

conflicts.description: title_akas declares no primary key, although the pair (titleid, ordering) is the natural unique identifier.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted the composite natural key (title_id, ordering) as the primary key of 'title_alternative'.

conflicts.description: Several IMDb tables declare no primary key at all, despite having natural keys (tconst, or tconst+ordering).
conflicts.resolution: Natural keys are inferred: title_episode and title_rating use title_id; title_credit uses a synthetic surrogate key because its natural key spans unpivoted sources.

conflicts.description: Primary-key conventions differ: IMDb uses alphanumeric natural keys (typed as number) while Sakila uses integer surrogate keys (typed as string).
conflicts.resolution: Both key styles are unified as 'string' identifiers, and merged entities reuse them (title_id, person_id).

conflicts.description: Sakila bridge tables declare no primary key even though (film_id, actor_id) and (film_id, category_id) are unique.
conflicts.resolution: Composite primary keys are declared on the corresponding bridge resources (title_genre; title_credit exposed via a surrogate key).

conflicts.description: payment declares payment_id but does not mark it as the primary key, while rental does mark rental_id.
conflicts.resolution: payment_id is adopted as the primary key of 'payment'.

conflicts.description: Merging entities from two independent sources produces several source primary keys feeding one target key.
conflicts.resolution: The unified 'person' and 'title' primary keys list all contributing source primary keys in their provenance.
